chunks: But the factions differed among themselves. Woe alas to the sinners for the torment of the grievous Day!

key_terms.الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا: Those who wronged themselves through disbelief or sin
key_terms.الْأَحْزَابُ: Factions or parties, referring to groups that divided religiously or politically
key_terms.فَوَيْلٌ: Woe or destruction, an expression of severe warning
key_terms.يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ: A painful Day, referring to the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Woe to those who wronged' in the context of sectarian division?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the post-Prophetic schism, where the 'factions' (ahzab) refer to the emerging political and theological groups that diverged from the Ahl al-Bayt's guidance. The 'painful punishment' serves as a warning against the injustice (zulm) of clinging to partisan interests over divine unity, a theme central to the concept of Wilayah. This division is viewed not merely as political but as a spiritual deviation that alienates believers from the true path of Imamate.
